Anna: Quick question — we started the canary for the new routing opt but there's a gap in the flag precedence docs. who wins: a route-level override, or a model-level override pinned by model-version?
Kevin: Route-level should be higher imo, but I remember an exception for emergency 'force-off' flags.
Miguel: Yeah, the usual rule we've been using is: explicit route override > model override > project > org default. force-off is a separate actor that trumps enable unless it's a soft block.
Sophia: Can you show a compact example? I'm trying to map this to the rollout we're about to do for search-v2.
Anna: Sure — here is the scenario: org default = enabled, project X sets disabled, model v2 sets enabled, route '/search' sets disabled. Which applies?
Miguel: In that stack, route '/search' (disabled) wins, so the route will see disabled. The model-level enable doesn't apply because route has a more specific scope.
Kevin: What about canary audiences? If route is disabled globally but we want a 10% canary to see model v2 enabled, can we scope a canary at route+audience?
Sam: Yes — audience-scoped overrides are treated as even more specific than route-level global overrides. precedence (most specific -> least): route+audience > route > model+audience > model > project > org.
Anna: That helps. So to run a 10% canary on /search we should create a route+audience override that enables the flag for that audience.
Sophia: Important note for rollout ops: the console UI currently shows model overrides separately — people might miss the audience-scoped route override. we should add a warning banner when a less-specific override would be shadowed.
Miguel: Agreed. Also watch out for the "force-off" behavior — DeployBot will annotate a flag as force-off during incidents and that always blocks other enables unless the flag config sets `allow_force_off=false`.
DeployBot: :information_source: Canary started for project-x on /search at 2312345690 (10% audience id: a-42). Tracking: rollout-id rlt-2026-1001.
Kevin: Thanks @DeployBot — FYI I'll open a tiny PR to the flag docs and add that concise precedence table and the UI banner proposal.
Anna: Awesome. @Sophia can you add a short ticket for the banner? label it "flag-ui" and link the canary id.
Sophia: Yep — created ticket PLAT-4456, added notes and repro steps.
Sam: One more gotcha: if project-level policy enforces `deny-route-overrides=true` then route overrides are ignored. That's rare but exists for regulated projects.
Miguel: Good point. That flips precedence because it's a policy constraint. We should call that out in the docs as "policy-level constraints may disable more specific overrides."
Anna: Perfect. I'm unblocking the rollout now that we have the doc + ticket. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
